# Native Marker Forward Kinematics From Replay States

## Scope and Evidence Boundary

F09d (#11907) maps a validated native replay's actual model configurations to
3-D marker positions by each engine's own forward kinematics. It does not
interpret coordinates as markers, resimulate the replay, score observations,
or qualify a model. A marker is a named point attached to an explicitly named
native body or frame by a finite local offset in metres.

## Mapping Contract

For output sample $i$ and ordered marker $j$, the engine evaluates the native
body/frame transform $T_{w b_j}(q_i)$ and local marker point $r_j$:

$$
p_{ij}^{w} = T_{w b_j}(q_i)\begin{bmatrix}r_j\\1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The mapping binds stable marker labels, exact native frame identifiers,
body-local offsets, output frame, simulation-relative timebase, source and
loaded-model digests, engine/provider identity, and the ordered mapping digest.
The resulting array has shape $(N, K, 3)$ and preserves the replay's actual
native output clock. Unknown frames, stale model/provider identity, duplicate
labels, invalid offsets, non-finite values, or incomplete output horizons fail
closed.

## Current Native Consumers

MuJoCo computes each position with the loaded model's forward pass and body
pose. Drake sets each replay configuration in its loaded plant context and
evaluates named frame points in world. Pinocchio F09e uses the existing native
replay adapter and `PinocchioPhysicsEngine` frame transforms, retaining complete
q/v with distinct `nq` and `nv`. All use the same loaded model identity that
was admitted by the native replay bundle. A separate native output
receipt binds F09c state/input/policy evidence to the marker-map and position
digests. This receipt remains unqualified.

The report retains every registered model/variant/drive cell and all six
required engines. Missing maps, unsupported providers, unavailable runtimes,
and rejected identities remain blockers. Full FK coverage means only that
every required row produced named positions; it does not promote model
qualification or establish observation agreement.

OpenSim geometry mapping belongs to F07 (#11903) and may be consumed here only
when its adapter supports the same complete replay state and model identity.
MyoSuite and Simscape remain visible and blocking until native providers are
implemented. No synthetic marker map is inferred from `q`, quaternions, mesh
vertices, coordinate names, or a capture.

## Synthetic Verification

Independent fixtures use a floating-base model, nonzero generalized
configuration, and nonzero body-local marker offset. The MuJoCo fixture uses
analytic quaternion and hinge rotations for the expected world point. The
Drake fixture compares its point result against the independent composition
of the native body's world pose and local offset while preserving $n_q\ne n_v$.
The Pinocchio 4.1 fixture independently composes a nonzero free-flyer pose,
revolute hinge, joint-origin transform, and frame-local marker offset while
preserving $n_q=8$, $n_v=7$.
These fixtures test software integration and identity checks only; they do not
establish anatomical marker attachment, observation fit, contact behavior,
muscle physiology, or scientific acceptance.

The calculation registry remains empty and manual release remains blocked.
